Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex EV Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. We ask that you limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex EV Inc.'s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jordan Hale, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; Mike Torres, Chief Manufacturing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 2024 was a strong quarter for Apex EV Inc. We made significant progress in several key areas, including expanding gross margins per vehicle through manufacturing efficiencies and cost reductions, refining our gross margin guidance with clear assumptions on volume ramps and regional dynamics, setting ambitious revenue targets for Q4 and FY25 amid delivery growth, achieving meaningful electric vehicle range improvements and efficiency gains that enhance customer value, and scaling revenue from software and services like subscriptions and autonomous driving features. The demand for our new Apex X crossover continues to be strong, and we are working diligently to increase production capacity to meet that demand. The impact of this product lineup is exceeding our initial expectations, driving market share gains in premium segments.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. Good morning, everyone. For Q3 2024, our revenue was $5.9 billion, representing a 35% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 22.4%, reflecting our ongoing efforts to improve operational efficiency. Our operating expenses were $1.3 billion, and net income was $520 million. We continue to maintain a healthy balance sheet with $9.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our guidance for the next quarter is revenue of $6.5 to $6.8 billion and gross margins of 24% to 26%.

As we dive deeper into the financials, I'd like to spend some time on one of our key performance indicators: gross margin per vehicle. This metric is the lifeblood of our automotive gross profit line, calculated as average selling price, or ASP, per vehicle minus cost of goods sold, or COGS, per vehicle. It's a volume-agnostic measure that strips out the noise of delivery fluctuations and really highlights our manufacturing efficiency, product mix, and pricing power in this hyper-competitive EV landscape.

In Q3, we delivered a record gross margin per vehicle of $14,200, up 28% year-over-year from $11,100 in Q3 2023 and 7% sequentially from $13,300 in Q2 2024. This puts our overall automotive gross margin at 22.4% for the quarter, expanding 450 basis points YoY and marking our sixth straight quarter of sequential improvement. For context, this outperforms the industry average of around 18% for mass-market EVs—think Rivian's recent 14-16% range or legacy OEMs like Ford's Model e segment scraping single digits amid their F-150 Lightning ramp-up challenges.

Let me break down the drivers here, starting with the topline. Our ASP held steady at $52,800 per vehicle, reflecting a favorable mix shift toward our higher-content Apex S sedan and the newly launched Apex X crossover, which carried an ASP premium of 15% over our volume Apex M platform. We saw 62% of deliveries from these premium SKUs, up from 48% a year ago, bolstered by strong demand for our UltraRange battery pack option—our 100 kWh LFP/NMC blend that's now standard on X models. Pricing discipline was key; despite aggressive IRA-compliant leasing incentives in the US, we avoided deep haircuts, with only a 2% concession versus 5-7% discounts from competitors like the Hyundai Ioniq 5 or VW ID.4 in Europe.

On the cost side, COGS per vehicle came in at $38,600, a 22% reduction YoY driven by structural tailwinds. Battery costs, which make up 38% of our bill of materials, or BOM, dropped to $112 per kWh at the pack level—down from $145/kWh last year—thanks to our Phase 2 vertical integration at our Nevada Gigafactory. We're now producing 70% of our 4680-style cylindrical cells in-house, mirroring Tesla's playbook but with a twist: our silicon-doped anodes yield 12% higher energy density at 5% lower cost than prismatic LFP cells flooding the market from CATL suppliers. This shaved $1,800 off per-vehicle battery COGS alone.

Manufacturing leverage was another big win. Our Fremont-adjacent Apex 2.0 line hit 85% OEE, or overall equipment effectiveness, up from 72% YoY, thanks to AI-optimized robotic sequencing that reduced structural welds by 25% and cut gigacasting cycle times to 45 seconds per underbody—on par with Tesla's Giga presses but scaled for our 250,000-unit capacity. Fixed platform costs, like our Apex Common Modular Architecture, amortized beautifully over 112,000 Q3 deliveries, dropping content cost per vehicle by $900. We also clawed back $450 per unit in supply chain efficiencies, negotiating 18% spot reductions on rare earths amid softening neodymium prices and dual-sourcing neo magnets from MP Materials in the US to de-risk China exposure.

Regionally, the story varies. In North America, which was 68% of volume, margins hit $15,400 per vehicle—juiced by $7,500 average IRA tax credits flowing straight to our leasing program, effectively boosting realized ASP by 14%. Europe, at 22% of mix, lagged at $12,100 due to VAT rebates and softer pricing against BYD's Seagull onslaught, but our Berlin plant's localization—now 65% EU-sourced content—dodged 10% Section 301 tariffs and improved to positive margins from last year's breakeven. China, our 10% wildcard at $11,800, faced brutal comps from Xiaomi's SU7 and Li Auto's L6, but our Shanghai JV with BAIC is ramping structural battery packs, targeting $10k/kWh parity by Q1 2025.

Strategically, these trends underscore our 'Scale or Sell' mantra. We're on track for $16,000+ per vehicle in Q4 as Apex X volumes hit 40k units and we layer in HW4 autonomy hardware—a $2,500 upcharge with 90% take rates projected. Long-term, our 2025-2027 roadmap pencils $18k-$20k margins at 500k annual run rate, funded by $1.2B in FCF this year. Initiatives like dry electrode coating pilots (cutting slurry costs 30%) and unboxed process assembly (à la Tesla's Cybercab) will drive 10-15% annual COGS deflation. Risks? Supply chain snarls on 8-layer PCBAs for our 800V architecture and potential US-China tariff hikes could pressure 200-300bps, but our 3:1 US-to-China sourcing ratio hedges that.

Overall, gross margin per vehicle is our North Star—proof we're not just shipping metal and batteries, but delivering shareholder value in an industry where 70% of OEMs are still underwater.

Turning to our gross margin outlook, we delivered a company gross margin of 22.4% in Q3, up significantly from prior periods, driven by production efficiencies at our Nevada Gigafactory, a favorable model mix skewed toward our high-margin Apex SUV, and the full realization of U.S. Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) production tax credits, which added approximately 450 basis points to our automotive gross margin.

Looking ahead, we are guiding for Q4 consolidated gross margins of 24% to 26%, representing a notable expansion quarter-over-quarter. For the full fiscal year 2024, we now expect consolidated gross margins of 23% to 25%, a meaningful step-up from prior expectations. Automotive gross margins specifically are projected at 24% to 26% for FY24, excluding regulatory credits, which we conservatively forecast at $1.5 billion for the year.

Let me walk you through the key assumptions underpinning this guidance, which reflect our disciplined cost management, vertical integration strategy, and resilience amid a dynamic EV market.

First, on volume and factory utilization ramp: We assume Q4 vehicle deliveries of 140,000 to 150,000 units, a 25% to 35% sequential increase, supported by the ongoing ramp of our Apex X at our Texas Gigafactory. At 85% utilization in Q4—up from 80% in Q3—we expect meaningful fixed cost leverage. Our structural battery pack design reduces bill-of-materials costs by 15% versus prior architectures, enabling sub-$100/kWh cell costs at scale.

Second, average selling price and mix dynamics: Q4 ASP guidance is $53,000 to $55,000 per vehicle, slightly up sequentially due to a richer mix: 60% premium models like the Apex SUV and new truck variants, versus 40% volume platforms. We're assuming no material ASP erosion, though noting competitive pressures in entry-level segments. Regulatory credits remain a tailwind at around $900 per vehicle.

Third, cost of goods sold reductions: Core COGS per unit is expected to decline to $37,000 to $39,000 in Q4, driven by battery costs locking in long-term LFP cathode contracts at $60/kWh, down significantly YoY, supplemented by our in-house cell production. Semiconductor normalization and manufacturing efficiencies from AI-driven automation target 25% labor cost reduction, with giga-press die-casting cutting SKU count by 40%.

Regionally: North America, 75% of Q4 volume, benefits from IRA credits at ~$7,500 per U.S.-built vehicle. Europe sees EU tariffs protecting margins, with Berlin ramp adding capacity. China delivers solid local margins via joint ventures.

Our margin expansion is underpinned by vertical integration: By FY25, in-house components will target 28% automotive gross margins. Key initiatives include software contributions, and risks like lithium prices are hedged. This reflects years of cost discipline in a tough market.

Before moving on, a quick note on our software and services segment, which is proving to be the high-margin engine accelerating our path to sustainable profitability. This segment—encompassing subscriptions for Full Autonomy Suite, OTA feature unlocks, premium connectivity, infotainment upgrades, and emerging robotaxi services—generated $1.45 billion in Q3 revenue, marking a 162% year-over-year increase from Q2 2023 levels. That's up 28% quarter-over-quarter.

Software and services now represent 5.8% of our total quarterly revenue, a significant jump from prior periods. Gross margins here remain industry-leading at 78.2%, thanks to the near-zero marginal cost of digital delivery. This recurring revenue stream is contributing over 15% to our adjusted EBITDA, underscoring our shift toward a software-defined vehicle model.

Breaking it down: Subscriptions and recurring services drove the lion's share at $875 million, with our flagship FAS subscription—Level 2+ to Level 3 autonomy—hitting 2.8 million active subscribers globally, ARPU at $42 per month. Premium connectivity added meaningfully. Autonomy unlocks surged with FSD Beta rollouts, yielding high conversion rates via our multi-sensor fusion. Robotaxi pilots and energy services rounded out emerging growth.

Regionally, North America led with strong adoption, China outpaced the market, Europe ramped pilots, and rest-of-world emerged. Trends like rising attachment rates and data flywheels fuel this, with Q4 guidance embedding further investments for unsupervised FSD and robotaxi scaling. Long-term, we see this eclipsing 20% of revenue by 2026 at 85%+ margins.

Finally, on forward revenue guidance: For Q4 2024, we expect total revenue of $6.5 to $6.8 billion, representing 21% to 25% sequential growth from Q3 and 35% to 40% year-over-year. This assumes 140,000 to 150,000 vehicle deliveries, with ASP at $72,000 to $75,000, reflecting mix shift to higher-margin pickups like our QuantumForge equivalent in the Apex lineup.

Automotive revenue at $5.8 to $6.1 billion, fueled by North American growth via IRA credits and fleet demand. Regulatory credits and services add $400 to $500 million.

For FY25, raising outlook to $26 to $28 billion, 44% to 56% over FY24, with 280,000 to 310,000 deliveries at $75,000 to $78,000 ASP. North America drives majority, Europe navigates tariffs with local assembly, Asia-Pacific emerges via JVs.

Strategic enablers include vertical integration, R&D in inverters and autonomy, supply chain resilience. Risks like macro softening are offset by strong liquidity.

I'll now turn the call over to Mike Torres to provide an update on our manufacturing operations.

Mike Torres:
Thank you, Sarah. We are pleased with the progress we've made in scaling up production of the Apex X. We delivered 112,000 vehicles in Q3, and our factories operated at high utilization rates. In particular, our fleet-wide average EPA range across models improved by 18% year-over-year to 412 miles, outpacing industry growth, with real-world efficiency at 2.4 mi/kWh—22% better than benchmarks. These gains stem from our Gen 3 Aether battery at 312 Wh/kg, 800V Titan architecture enabling ultra-fast charging, and aero/lightweighting like 0.23 Cd on the SUV.

Tailored regionally: North America captures share via IRA-eligible content, Europe exceeds WLTP targets, China edges locals on efficiency. These improvements compress COGS per mile, lifting margins, with R&D committed to solid-state for 450 Wh/kg by 2027. Q4 embeds 20% range uplift, supporting 35% delivery growth.

We are implementing several initiatives to further improve our manufacturing efficiency and reduce costs, including AI robotics, gigacasting, and supply chain dual-sourcing. We are on track to meet our production targets for the year.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from the line of John Mayer with Goldman Sachs.

Analyst 1:
Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. On gross margin per vehicle, can you elaborate more on the regional variances and how you're mitigating tariff risks heading into Q4?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, John. As I detailed, North America led at $15,400 per vehicle thanks to IRA credits boosting effective ASP. Europe improved to $12,100 with Berlin localization dodging tariffs, and China held at $11,800 amid comps but ramping structural packs. Our 3:1 US-to-China sourcing hedges tariff hikes, and initiatives like neo magnet dual-sourcing from MP Materials de-risk further. We're confident in $16,000+ in Q4.

Operator:
Our next question from Emily Chen at Morgan Stanley.

Analyst 2:
Great, thanks. For gross margin guidance, what are the biggest assumptions around COGS reductions, and how sensitive is it to lithium prices?

Sarah Chen:
Emily, key COGS drivers include battery contracts at $55-60/kWh via CATL and in-house 4680s, semiconductor normalization, and 25% labor cuts from AI welding. We've hedged 70% of lithium at $12k/tonne, mitigating spot spikes above $15k. Utilization above 80% leverages fixed costs like Tesla's ramps. Risks are contained, positioning for the high end of 24-26% in Q4.

Operator:
Next from David Kim with JPMorgan.

Analyst 3:
Thanks. Mike, on manufacturing, how are range and efficiency gains translating to line rates, and any updates on gigafactory expansions?

Mike Torres:
David, efficiency like 96.5% inverter peaks and 28% regen recapture directly boost OEE to 85%, cutting cycle times with AI sequencing and 45-second gigacasting. Nevada Phase 2 hits 80 GWh run-rate for cells, Texas ramps Apex X to 40k units. Expansions on track, with $2.5B CapEx for second giga line, enabling FY25 targets.

Operator:
Our next question from Lisa Patel at Barclays.

Analyst 4:
Thanks, team. Jordan, on the big picture, how does software/services growth factor into your revenue guidance for FY25, especially robotaxi?

Jordan Hale:
Lisa, software at $1.45B this quarter, 162% YoY, scales to $6-7B FY24 and 20%+ of FY25 revenue at 85% margins. FAS subs at 2.8M users, unlocks converting at 14%, robotaxi pilots logging millions of miles toward L4 in China Q4. It redefines economics, with B2B fleets like Uber adding predictability to our $26-28B FY25 guide.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more.

Operator:
Our final question from Robert Lee at Citi.

Analyst 5:
Congrats again. Sarah, walking through FY25 revenue regional breakdown and key technical initiatives supporting it?

Sarah Chen:
Robert, North America $18-19B on 55% growth, IRA localization, 8% premium share. Europe $5-6B navigating CO2 penalties with German assembly. APAC $2.5-3B via Shanghai JV, ADAS differentiation. Tech like silicon-carbide inverters for 15-min charges, Mobileye autonomy, 20% PHEV mix, 85% NA cathodes. $12B liquidity funds execution despite macro risks.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Jordan Hale for closing remarks.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Apex EV Inc. Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
